skill.name: infrastructure
skill.description: Provides infrastructure-as-code patterns for deploying Guts nodes with Terraform, Docker, Docker Compose, and Kubernetes.
skill.summary: Plan Guts node deployments with practical Terraform, Docker, and Kubernetes examples.
skill.author: AbdelStark

security_audit.summary: All static external-command findings are Markdown code fences or infrastructure examples in SKILL.md, not executable Ruby backticks. The system-reconnaissance finding is a Terraform AMI reference inside a sample resource. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or hidden operational behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Markdown code fences triggered command-execution heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as non-executable templates and avoid ambiguous bare fences when a language tag is available.
Add a short note that users must review providers, variables, secrets, and policies before production use.

remediation.issue: Some container and Kubernetes examples use mutable image references.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer pinned image versions or digests in production examples to improve reproducibility.

content.value_statement: Deploying Guts nodes requires consistent Terraform, Docker, and Kubernetes patterns. This skill provides reusable infrastructure examples for local, test, and production environments.
actual_capabilities: Outlines Terraform module folders for development, staging, and production environments.
Shows a sample Terraform node module with node count, instance type, and tags.
Provides a multi-stage Dockerfile pattern for building a Guts node binary.
Defines a Docker Compose pattern for three local Guts nodes with peer settings.
Provides a Kubernetes StatefulSet pattern with ports, persistent storage, and replicas.
Lists monitoring and security checklist areas for production planning.
limitations: Examples are templates and are not complete deployment projects.
The Terraform sample is AWS-focused despite the broader cloud-agnostic goal.
Secrets, TLS, RBAC, and network policies are listed but not fully implemented.
Users must adapt versions, resource sizes, storage, and policies for their environment.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap Local Node Testing
use_cases.description: Create a Docker Compose plan for several Guts nodes with peer settings and persistent data volumes.

use_cases.title: Plan Cloud Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Draft Terraform module structure and resource patterns before building a deployable environment.

use_cases.title: Prepare Kubernetes Deployment
use_cases.description: Design a StatefulSet-based node deployment with stable identities, storage claims, and exposed service ports.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Local Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a local Docker Compose setup for three Guts nodes. Include peer settings, ports, and data volumes.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Terraform Modules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a Terraform folder structure and module plan for dev, staging, and prod Guts node environments.

prompt_templates.title: Create Kubernetes Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a Kubernetes StatefulSet deployment for Guts nodes. Include replicas, ports, persistent storage, and operational notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review a Guts infrastructure design for production readiness. Focus on monitoring, TLS, secrets, network policies, and RBAC.

output_examples.input: Plan a local three-node Guts environment.
output_examples.output: A concise deployment outline with three node services, API and peer ports, shared peer configuration, and persistent data volumes.

output_examples.input: Design the Terraform layout for a staging environment.
output_examples.output: A module-oriented structure with network, compute, and storage areas, plus variables for node count and instance sizing.

output_examples.input: Check whether the Kubernetes plan is production ready.
output_examples.output: A readiness review covering persistent storage, exposed ports, monitoring, TLS certificates, secrets handling, RBAC, and network isolation.

best_practices: Treat all examples as starting points and validate them against your cloud account, cluster, and security policy.
Pin image versions, review base images, and scan generated artifacts before deployment.
Add secrets management, TLS, RBAC, monitoring, and network policies before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not copy example manifests directly into production without environment-specific review.
Do not store secrets in Docker Compose files, Terraform variables, or Kubernetes manifests.
Do not rely on mutable image tags for regulated or high-availability deployments.

faq.question: What does this skill help me deploy?
faq.answer: It helps plan infrastructure patterns for Guts nodes across Docker, Terraform, and Kubernetes environments.

faq.question: Does it create a complete production stack?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and checklists that users must adapt and complete for their own environment.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it execute deployment commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains documentation examples and does not run Terraform, Docker, or Kubernetes commands.

faq.question: What security areas does it mention?
faq.answer: It mentions TLS certificates, network policies, external secrets, security scanning, and Kubernetes RBAC.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is useful for developers, infrastructure engineers, and platform teams planning Guts node deployments.
